description:
At pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs:375-403:

  /// ...could not locate a certificate in the caller-supplied bundle...
  CrlSignerNotFound,

  /// ...found a candidate cert in the bundle, but the candidate does not chain back to a self-signed (anchor-like) cert...
  CrlSignerNotTrusted,

Both variants are unit (no fields). The contract gives callers no way to tell, programmatically:

1. For CrlSignerNotFound: which AKI/DN was searched for. A caller diagnosing 'why didn't my bundle work?' has to log the CRL DER themselves and re-parse the AKI/issuer DN, or rebuild the search themselves. No information about whether the AKI was present-but-no-match vs. absent vs. present-but-malformed.

2. For CrlSignerNotTrusted: which candidate was found (so the caller could log 'I tried this cert but it didn't reach an anchor'). The caller cannot distinguish 'discovery found cert X but X's issuer is missing from the bundle' from 'discovery found cert X but X is in a cycle' from 'discovery found cert X but the walk hit max_steps without finding a self-signed terminator.'

Defensive-code-forcing aspect: a caller who wants production-quality diagnostic output (the kind that gets file an issue against pkix-revocation if the message is opaque) must:

  - re-parse the CRL to extract the AKI/issuer DN
  - re-implement discover_crl_signer to find the candidate
  - re-implement reaches_self_signed (and they CAN'T, it's pub(crate) — see PKIX-lnnl.16)
  - log all of the above as ad-hoc strings

A richer error shape would be something like:

  CrlSignerNotFound { searched_aki: Option<Vec<u8>>, searched_issuer_dn: Vec<u8> },
  CrlSignerNotTrusted { candidate_subject_dn: Vec<u8>, candidate_serial: SerialNumber, walked_steps: u32 },

But that runs into:
- no_std vs alloc considerations (Vec<u8>)
- whether pkix-revocation Error should ever carry per-error context payloads
- consistency with the rest of Error variants (most are unit; only Revoked carries data)
- size of Error (currently quite small)

Counter-argument: existing Error variants in pkix-revocation are mostly unit-shaped. CrlParseError(DerError) and OcspParseError(DerError) and Revoked are the only ones with payloads. Adding payload to the discovery errors would be a precedent that other variants in this module would feel pressure to match.

Recommendation: file (this issue) for visibility, then pick one of:

(A) Status quo: unit variants, document explicitly in the rustdoc 'this error carries no payload; callers needing detailed diagnostics must invoke discover_crl_signer directly (currently pub) and inspect.' This requires resolving PKIX-lnnl.16 in the FULL-LOW-LEVEL direction.

(B) Add payload fields, accept the precedent, plan a follow-up to enrich other Error variants similarly.

(C) Pull-the-trigger compromise: introduce a single new variant `CrlSignerDiscoveryFailed { stage: DiscoveryStage }` with a small enum DiscoveryStage { Aki, Dn, AnchorWalk } describing how far it got. Keeps payload bounded.

This is api-contract,underspecified because the as-shipped contract leaves callers without the diagnostic surface they need at runtime.

Acceptance: a decision recorded. If (A), one-line rustdoc addition is the fix.
title: CrlSignerNotFound vs CrlSignerNotTrusted carry no payload identifying which signer failed
